bail.regulator: California Department of Insurance (bail agents are licensed by CDI)
how_to_verify: Ask the bail agent for their CDI license number and their Bail Identification card (CDI issues one to every individual bail licensee).
Open CDI's 'Check a License' tool at https://cdicloud.insurance.ca.gov/cal (use Edge, Chrome, Safari or Firefox).
Choose 'License Number Search' and enter the 6–8 character license number with no spaces — or use 'Individual Name Search' / 'Business Name Search'.
Open the result and confirm the license is active and shows a bail license type; check the discipline history on the record.
Active status is only valid if the licensee also has a valid bail bond and surety appointment on file — the record's appointment details should show this.
Questions about a bail license: CDI Bail Unit, (916) 492-3035, sac.bail@insurance.ca.gov.
consumer_tips: Each surety company must file its bail rates with CDI, and agents for that surety must charge the filed rate. The cost is most commonly 10% of the bond amount plus actual, necessary and reasonable expenses; an agent may charge less by rebating (Prop. 103).
Bail premiums are nonrefundable, even if charges are dropped or never filed. Exception: if the defendant is surrendered, the fee is refundable minus administrative costs (CCR Title 10 §2090).
Charging a renewal premium is illegal since January 1, 2022 (Penal Code 1276.1).
Bail agents cannot surrender a defendant back into custody for nonpayment of premium.

Collateral and liens are not released until the bail is paid, the case is settled and the bond is exonerated (see CCR Title 10 §§2088.2, 2088.3, 2089). todo: CDI pages loaded did not address written receipts — confirm receipt rules before stating them.

Bail agents may not solicit business; you (the arrestee, their attorney, or an adult friend/family member) must contact them. Solicitation inside courts, jails and police stations is prohibited — avoid agents who approach you there or inmates who push a specific agent.
Watch for fake jail or government websites set up by bail agents; double-check the URL before entering defendant information.
File a complaint or ask questions with CDI: 1-800-927-4357.
